# Bashref 2.1.0

Bashref 2.1.0 extends the bilingual Bash reference product with standalone executables and stronger operational support.

## Installation

For a no-Python standalone installation, download the archive for your platform from this release. Python users can install the wheel:

```bash
pipx install https://github.com/MMKarii/bash-fa-reference/releases/download/v2.1.0/bashref-2.1.0-py3-none-any.whl
```

Verify any installation:

```bash
bashref --version
bashref doctor
bashref search quoting
```

## Highlights

- single-file standalone executable for Linux x86_64
- standalone macOS executables for Apple Silicon and Intel
- standalone Windows x86_64 executable
- `bashref doctor` runtime/reference diagnostics
- concise command summary with `bashref usage` or no arguments
- compatibility matrix, troubleshooting, FAQ, support and uninstall guidance
- standalone binaries smoke-tested on their native GitHub Actions runners
- v2.0 documentation snapshot kept immutable while v2.1 gets its own stable snapshot

## Artifacts

The release includes:

- `bashref-2.1.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`
- `bashref-2.1.0-macos-arm64.tar.gz`
- `bashref-2.1.0-macos-x86_64.tar.gz`
- `bashref-2.1.0-windows-x86_64.zip`
- `bashref-2.1.0-py3-none-any.whl`
- `bashref-2.1.0.tar.gz`
- `bashref_2.1.0_all.deb`
- RPM package
- portable, man-page, completion and documentation archives
- Homebrew formula
- `SHA256SUMS`

## Checksums

Download the desired artifacts and `SHA256SUMS`, then verify on systems with GNU coreutils:

```bash
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
```

## Upgrade from v2.0

Existing v2 CLI commands, structured reference IDs, exit-code contracts, and JSON lookup output remain compatible. v2.1 adds standalone distribution and diagnostics without removing the wheel, Linux packages, man pages, or v2.0 documentation snapshot.
